rendered: The review that discusses DRX (disordered rock-salt) cathodes in depth is the Adv. Energy Mater. review on next-generation cobalt-free cathodes (aenm-2022), whose section on DRX cathodes is headed "5. DRX Cathodes[1]". The paper does not state a reference count for DRX. Counting the reference-list entries its DRX citations point to, the total is 11[2] references, running from reference 34[3] ("[34] R. J. Clément, Z. Lun, G. Ceder, Energy Environ. Sci. 2020, 13, 345.[4]") to reference 44[5] ("[44] A. Abdellahi, A. Urban, S. Dacek, G. Ceder, Chem. Mater. 2016, 28, 5373.[6]"). Citations outside that run, such as the general reference on Li/TM ordering and the software citation for the DRX structure figure, are not counted as DRX references. The other reviews in the collection (ensm-2020, mattod-2020, and ensm-2021) do not discuss DRX cathodes with references; ensm-2021 mentions a "disordered rock[7]" cathode type only in passing, in a list of advanced cathodes.
